## 1. Blunt verdict
The registered 28-file corpus is real, internally consistent, and genuinely drift-gated (baseline full_gate:53-55: `fixtures: PASS`, "no drift — 55 file(s) verified"). But the doc's blanket provenance sentence — "Every file under generated/ and expectations/ is authored in-tree by the deterministic generator" — is FALSE for the majority of the tree it names: ~91 additional fixture files sit under generated/ and sibling dirs (hls/, mjpeg_h3/, generated/ivf/) with no manifest rows, no generator coverage, and no drift gate. The layout section does not mention three of the directories that exist. A licensing ledger that understates its own coverage by ~75% is a compliance defect, not a typo.

## 3. Contradictions
| This doc says | Other source says | Which is true (proof) |
|---|---|---|
| "Every file under generated/ ... authored in-tree by the deterministic generator" | MANIFEST.toml `file_count = 28` vs 116 files under generated/ (33+81+2) | The manifest is the truth: only 28 are generator-accounted; the doc's sentence overstates coverage (ls counts this run) |
| Layout lists generated/{valid,malformed}, MANIFEST.toml, expectations/ | Actual tree also has generated/ivf/ (2 files), hls/ (3 dirs), mjpeg_h3/ (4 files) | ls of tests/fixtures — the doc omits three directories entirely |

## 4. Fabrication / inflation indicators
- The doc presents itself as THE corpus licensing ledger while covering 28 of ~140 fixture files under tests/fixtures (~20-25% by file count); W16-A02's independent count ("~75% of the committed corpus is UNREGISTERED") agrees with mine.
- The class-D "none" claim coexists with an unregistered hls/ tree whose segments have unknown (possibly third-party) provenance — the exact category the ledger exists to rule out.
- The 28-row table is precise and honest about what it covers; the dishonesty is the blanket scoping sentences around it.
